## Purpose

This is the shared data-preparation file for the next phase of the project. It creates analysis-ready local files from the two source files already stored in this project:

- `h1bdataset_new.csv`: one H-1B lottery registration per row.
- `compustat_raw_2019_2023.xlsx`: Compustat firm-year accounts.

The primary output is an H-1B **firm-lottery-year** panel. It contains the lottery-luck and next-year participation variables, measures of approved petitions by education, and—where an EIN links to Compustat—sector and firm-productivity variables. No download is required to rebuild it.

The notebook saves the following files under `data/`:

- `h1b_firm_year_analysis.rds`: preferred analysis file; preserves types.
- `h1b_firm_year_analysis.csv`: portable version for inspection or use outside R.
- `h1b_lottery_participation_panel.rds`: panel with next-year participation outcomes.
- `h1b_lottery_year_rates.csv`: year-level lottery probabilities used to define luck.

## Scope and interpretation

The lottery source identifies firms through employer EINs. The education field is generally observed only after selection/petition processing, not for the full pool of non-selected registrations. For that reason, education variables in this dataset are explicitly labelled as **approved-petition** counts and shares. They support descriptive worker-composition heterogeneity; they do not create degree-specific lottery shocks.

Compustat covers public firms only. Therefore, `sector`, sales per employee, and the TFP-style residual are missing for H-1B firms that do not link to Compustat. Sector-specific productivity analysis must be described as applying to the matched public-firm sample, whereas the lottery and participation analysis uses the full H-1B employer panel.

## Packages and paths

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)

raw_h1b_path <- "h1bdataset_new.csv"
raw_compustat_path <- "compustat_raw_2019_2023.xlsx"
# Rendered from the project root, save the shared files in `data/`; rendered
# from this file's own directory, save them beside this notebook.
derived_dir <- if (dir.exists("data")) "data" else "."
dir.create(derived_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

stopifnot(file.exists(raw_h1b_path), file.exists(raw_compustat_path))

clean_ein <- function(x) {
  x <- str_replace_all(as.character(x), "[^0-9]", "")
  x <- str_replace(x, "^0+", "")
  na_if(x, "")
}

clean_character <- function(x) {
  x |>
    as.character() |>
    str_squish() |>
    na_if("")
}

safe_divide <- function(numerator, denominator) {
  if_else(!is.na(denominator) & denominator > 0, numerator / denominator, NA_real_)
}

first_non_missing <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x) & x != ""]
  if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else x[[1]]
}

naics_sector <- function(naics) {
  code <- str_sub(str_replace_all(as.character(naics), "[^0-9]", ""), 1, 2)
  case_when(
    code == "11" ~ "Agriculture",
    code == "21" ~ "Mining, Oil, and Gas",
    code == "22" ~ "Utilities",
    code == "23" ~ "Construction",
    code %in% c("31", "32", "33") ~ "Manufacturing",
    code == "42" ~ "Wholesale Trade",
    code %in% c("44", "45") ~ "Retail Trade",
    code %in% c("48", "49") ~ "Transportation and Warehousing",
    code == "51" ~ "Information",
    code == "52" ~ "Finance and Insurance",
    code == "53" ~ "Real Estate",
    code == "54" ~ "Professional and Technical Services",
    code == "55" ~ "Management of Companies",
    code == "56" ~ "Administrative and Waste Services",
    code == "61" ~ "Education",
    code == "62" ~ "Health Care",
    code == "71" ~ "Arts and Recreation",
    code == "72" ~ "Accommodation and Food",
    code == "81" ~ "Other Services",
    code == "92" ~ "Public Administration",
    TRUE ~ "Unknown"
  )
}
```

## Build the H-1B firm-lottery-year panel

The estimation sample uses the standard registration statuses: `CREATED` in FY2021 and `ELIGIBLE` in later years, plus `SELECTED`. This excludes non-registration administrative records. `selection_shock` is actual selections less expected selections, where expectations use the national selection rate in the same lottery year.

```{r}
h1b_registration <- read_csv(
  raw_h1b_path,
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  col_select = c(
    fein, employer_name, lottery_year, status_type, first_decision,
    ben_multi_reg_ind, ed_level_definition
  ),
  na = c("", "NA"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  transmute(
    ein = clean_ein(fein),
    employer_name = clean_character(employer_name),
    lottery_year = parse_integer(lottery_year),
    status_type = clean_character(status_type),
    first_decision = clean_character(first_decision),
    selected = status_type == "SELECTED",
    # Most non-selected registrations have no petition decision. Treat the
    # absent decision as no approval so that firm-level approval counts are 0.
    approved = coalesce(first_decision == "Approved", FALSE),
    multiple_registration = case_when(
      ben_multi_reg_ind == "1" ~ TRUE,
      ben_multi_reg_ind == "0" ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ NA
    ),
    education_raw = clean_character(ed_level_definition),
    degree_group = case_when(
      education_raw == "DOCTORATE DEGREE" ~ "Doctorate",
      education_raw == "MASTER'S DEGREE" ~ "Master's",
      education_raw == "BACHELOR'S DEGREE" ~ "Bachelor's",
      is.na(education_raw) ~ "Missing degree",
      TRUE ~ "Other degree"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ein),
    !is.na(lottery_year),
    status_type %in% c("CREATED", "ELIGIBLE", "SELECTED")
  )

lottery_year_rates <- h1b_registration |>
  group_by(lottery_year) |>
  summarise(
    year_registrations = n(),
    year_selected = sum(selected),
    year_selection_rate = year_selected / year_registrations,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

h1b_firm_year <- h1b_registration |>
  group_by(ein, lottery_year) |>
  summarise(
    employer_name = first_non_missing(employer_name),
    n_registrations = n(),
    n_selected = sum(selected),
    n_approved = sum(approved),
    n_approved_bachelors = sum(approved & degree_group == "Bachelor's"),
    n_approved_masters = sum(approved & degree_group == "Master's"),
    n_approved_doctorate = sum(approved & degree_group == "Doctorate"),
    n_approved_other_degree = sum(approved & degree_group == "Other degree"),
    n_approved_missing_degree = sum(approved & degree_group == "Missing degree"),
    multiple_registration_share = if_else(
      all(is.na(multiple_registration)),
      NA_real_,
      mean(multiple_registration, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(lottery_year_rates, by = "lottery_year") |>
  mutate(
    expected_selected = n_registrations * year_selection_rate,
    selection_shock = n_selected - expected_selected,
    selection_rate = safe_divide(n_selected, n_registrations),
    selection_luck = safe_divide(selection_shock, n_registrations),
    selection_luck_10pp = selection_luck / 0.10,
    approval_rate_selected = safe_divide(n_approved, n_selected),
    approved_masters_share = safe_divide(n_approved_masters, n_approved),
    approved_doctorate_share = safe_divide(n_approved_doctorate, n_approved),
    approved_bachelors_share = safe_divide(n_approved_bachelors, n_approved)
  )
```

## Add next-year lottery participation outcomes

Absence from the next year's file is treated as zero registrations. The final observed lottery year is excluded because a next-year outcome is not yet available.

```{r}
next_year_registrations <- h1b_firm_year |>
  transmute(
    ein,
    lottery_year = lottery_year - 1L,
    next_year_registrations = n_registrations
  )

lottery_participation_panel <- h1b_firm_year |>
  filter(lottery_year < max(lottery_year_rates$lottery_year)) |>
  left_join(next_year_registrations, by = c("ein", "lottery_year")) |>
  mutate(
    next_year_registrations = replace_na(next_year_registrations, 0L),
    returns_next_year = as.integer(next_year_registrations > 0),
    log_current_registrations = log1p(n_registrations),
    log_next_year_registrations = log1p(next_year_registrations)
  )
```

## Add Compustat sector and productivity measures

Compustat reports sales in millions of dollars and employees in thousands, so `sales_per_employee_thousands` is in thousands of dollars per employee. The TFP-style measure is a residual from a descriptive production-function regression; it is included as a prepared outcome, not a causal estimate.

```{r}
compustat <- read_excel(raw_compustat_path) |>
  transmute(
    ein = clean_ein(`Employer Identification Number`),
    gvkey = clean_character(`Global Company Key`),
    fyear = as.integer(`Data Year - Fiscal`),
    company_name = clean_character(`Company Name`),
    naics = clean_character(`North American Industry Classification Code`),
    sector = naics_sector(`North American Industry Classification Code`),
    employees_thousands = as.numeric(Employees),
    sales_millions = as.numeric(`Sales/Turnover (Net)`),
    operating_income_millions = as.numeric(`Operating Income Before Depreciation`),
    capital_millions = as.numeric(`Property, Plant and Equipment - Total (Gross)`)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(ein), !is.na(fyear)) |>
  mutate(
    row_priority = coalesce(employees_thousands, 0) +
      coalesce(sales_millions, 0) / 1000000
  ) |>
  arrange(ein, fyear, desc(row_priority)) |>
  group_by(ein, fyear) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-row_priority) |>
  mutate(
    sales_per_employee_thousands = safe_divide(sales_millions, employees_thousands),
    operating_income_per_employee_thousands = safe_divide(
      operating_income_millions, employees_thousands
    )
  )

tfp_training_data <- compustat |>
  mutate(compustat_row_id = row_number()) |>
  filter(
    sales_millions > 0,
    employees_thousands > 0,
    capital_millions > 0,
    sector != "Unknown"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_sales = log(sales_millions),
    log_employees = log(employees_thousands),
    log_capital = log(capital_millions)
  )

tfp_model <- lm(
  log_sales ~ log_employees + log_capital + factor(fyear) + factor(sector),
  data = tfp_training_data
)

compustat <- compustat |>
  mutate(compustat_row_id = row_number()) |>
  left_join(
    tfp_training_data |>
      transmute(compustat_row_id, tfp_residual_proxy = residuals(tfp_model)),
    by = "compustat_row_id"
  ) |>
  select(-compustat_row_id)

h1b_firm_year_analysis <- h1b_firm_year |>
  left_join(compustat, by = c("ein", "lottery_year" = "fyear")) |>
  left_join(
    compustat |>
      transmute(
        ein,
        lottery_year = fyear - 1L,
        employees_thousands_next = employees_thousands,
        sales_per_employee_thousands_next = sales_per_employee_thousands,
        tfp_residual_proxy_next = tfp_residual_proxy
      ),
    by = c("ein", "lottery_year")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    compustat_ein_match = !is.na(gvkey),
    registrations_per_1000_employees = 1000 * safe_divide(n_registrations, employees_thousands),
    selected_per_1000_employees = 1000 * safe_divide(n_selected, employees_thousands),
    approved_per_1000_employees = 1000 * safe_divide(n_approved, employees_thousands),
    selection_shock_per_1000_employees = 1000 * safe_divide(selection_shock, employees_thousands),
    sales_per_employee_growth_next = if_else(
      sales_per_employee_thousands > 0 & sales_per_employee_thousands_next > 0,
      log(sales_per_employee_thousands_next) - log(sales_per_employee_thousands),
      NA_real_
    ),
    tfp_residual_change_next = tfp_residual_proxy_next - tfp_residual_proxy
  )
```

## Save and verify the shared local files

```{r}
saveRDS(
  h1b_firm_year_analysis,
  file.path(derived_dir, "h1b_firm_year_analysis.rds")
)
write_csv(
  h1b_firm_year_analysis,
  file.path(derived_dir, "h1b_firm_year_analysis.csv")
)
saveRDS(
  lottery_participation_panel,
  file.path(derived_dir, "h1b_lottery_participation_panel.rds")
)
write_csv(
  lottery_year_rates,
  file.path(derived_dir, "h1b_lottery_year_rates.csv")
)

stopifnot(
  file.exists(file.path(derived_dir, "h1b_firm_year_analysis.rds")),
  file.exists(file.path(derived_dir, "h1b_lottery_participation_panel.rds"))
)

tibble(
  dataset = c(
    "H-1B firm-lottery-year analysis panel",
    "Lottery next-year participation panel",
    "Lottery-year selection-rate file"
  ),
  rows = c(
    nrow(h1b_firm_year_analysis),
    nrow(lottery_participation_panel),
    nrow(lottery_year_rates)
  ),
  firms = c(
    n_distinct(h1b_firm_year_analysis$ein),
    n_distinct(lottery_participation_panel$ein),
    NA_integer_
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Variables for the next analysis files

| Question | Main variables | Important sample restriction |
|---|---|---|
| Lottery luck and later participation | `selection_luck_10pp`, `next_year_registrations`, `returns_next_year` | Use `h1b_lottery_participation_panel`; cluster by `ein`. |
| Firm heterogeneity by sector | `sector`, `selection_shock`, `approved_per_1000_employees` | Restrict to `compustat_ein_match` and a non-`Unknown` sector. |
| Worker-composition heterogeneity | `n_approved_bachelors`, `n_approved_masters`, `n_approved_doctorate` and their shares | Associational unless a degree-specific source of lottery variation is constructed. |
| Why firms may benefit | `sales_per_employee_growth_next`, `tfp_residual_change_next` | Public firms linked to Compustat; outcomes are firm-level, not domestic-worker outcomes. |

The next modeling notebook should read the `.rds` file rather than reconstructing these variables:

```{r eval=FALSE}
panel <- readRDS("data/h1b_firm_year_analysis.rds")
participation <- readRDS("data/h1b_lottery_participation_panel.rds")
```
